chunks.label: Casual goodbyes
chunks.rationale: Lets you say bye to friends, classmates and coworkers.
chunks.interference: Sayounara sounds final; with friends say mata ne or jaa mata.

chunks.label: Leaving and coming home
chunks.rationale: Lets you do the daily door greetings with family or coworkers.
chunks.interference: Each line has a fixed answer: tadaima gets okaeri, ittekimasu gets itterasshai; don't swap speakers.

chunks.label: Saying thank you
chunks.rationale: Lets you thank staff, friends and anyone who helped.
chunks.interference: Gozaimashita is for help already given; doumo alone can sound curt.
members: ありがとうございました

chunks.label: Replying to thanks
chunks.rationale: Lets you answer thanks, apologies or praise.
chunks.interference: Douitashimashite is textbook-stiff; most people say ie ie.

chunks.label: Saying sorry
chunks.rationale: Lets you apologize for being late, a slip or a mistake.
chunks.interference: Doumo sumimasen can be thanks as well as sorry; gomen gomen is too light for anything serious.
members: 遅くなってすみません

chunks.label: Greeting and meeting people
chunks.rationale: Lets you say good evening and handle the first questions with someone new.
chunks.interference: Youkoso welcomes you to a place, not into a shop (irasshaimase) or home (okaeri).

chunks.label: Catching up with friends
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask how someone has been and react when you meet again.
chunks.interference: Genki datta? needs a gap since you last met; saikin dou? works for people you see often.

chunks.label: See you again
chunks.rationale: Lets you say when you'll meet next.
chunks.interference: Mata kondo is often a polite no, not a real plan.

chunks.label: Time to go
chunks.rationale: Lets you wrap up a visit or leave work before others.
chunks.interference: Osaki ni also starts osaki ni douzo (after you); the situation decides.

chunks.label: Take care on parting
chunks.rationale: Lets you send someone off warmly and pass on greetings.
chunks.interference: Genki de ne implies a long parting; for an ordinary night say ki o tsukete kaette ne.

chunks.label: Small talk with neighbours
chunks.rationale: Lets you trade the weather and doorstep lines that open daily chats.
chunks.interference: Odekake desu ka isn't really asking where you're going.

chunks.label: Thanks for real help
chunks.rationale: Lets you thank people for help over time or for getting you out of a fix.
chunks.interference: Osewa ni narimashita is for endings; the ongoing osewa ni natte imasu is a work greeting.
members: いつもありがとうございます

chunks.label: Work greetings
chunks.rationale: Lets you greet coworkers and thank people for their work.
chunks.interference: Gokurousama only goes to people below you or service staff; to bosses say otsukaresama.

chunks.label: Welcoming a guest in
chunks.rationale: Lets you follow a host's welcome at the door and inside.
chunks.interference: Irasshai is a host's welcome; shop staff's irasshaimase needs no answer.

chunks.label: Guest and host courtesies
chunks.rationale: Lets you enter and leave a home politely and handle offers of food.
chunks.interference: Ojama shimasu is arriving and ojama shimashita leaving; enryo shinaide is the host, enryo naku the guest's reply.

chunks.label: Courtesy with strangers
chunks.rationale: Lets you make way, get off a packed train and excuse yourself politely.
chunks.interference: Shitsurei shimashita is sorry for a slip; shitsurei desu ga opens a question.

chunks.label: Formal apologies
chunks.rationale: Lets you apologize properly at work or to customers.
chunks.interference: Gozaimasen is staff-level formal; arimasen is enough for you.
members: お忙しいところすみません
ご迷惑をおかけしました

chunks.label: Work replies
chunks.rationale: Lets you answer requests and instructions politely at work or with staff.
chunks.interference: Kentou shimasu usually means no; shouchi shimashita is a firm yes.

chunks.label: Rough and pleading apologies
chunks.rationale: Lets you catch blunt or desperate apologies in casual talk and drama.
chunks.interference: Suman is masculine and casual; never use it upward.

chunks.label: Modest replies
chunks.rationale: Lets you answer praise and kind questions modestly.
chunks.interference: Mada mada desu is about yourself; mada mada da na said to someone else is a put-down.

Duplicate of ただいま (same phrase, kanji spelling).
